title: GPU Spot Fallback Autoscaler: Terraform Module + Operational Runbook
author: Leah Kim
body:
Overview:

This document describes the purpose, Terraform module API, CI/CD workflow, monitoring, and an operational runbook for the GPU Spot Fallback Autoscaler (GSFA) component. GSFA is a modular, reusable Terraform + controller pattern that allows Redwood clusters to prefer lower-cost spot (preemptible) GPU capacity and automatically fallback to on-demand or reserved capacity when spot supply is insufficient or interruption risk exceeds policy thresholds.

Goals:
- Reduce unit inference cost by preferring spot GPUs where safe.
- Maintain capacity SLOs for critical inference workloads by automatic, automated fallback to on-demand/dedicated pools.
- Provide a single, audited Terraform module for provisioning autoscaling groups, instance pools, IAM & networking artifacts and config for the controller.
- Provide a precise operational playbook for oncall and infra engineers.

Audience:
- Infra engineers operating GPU fleets
- Platform engineers integrating autoscaling in Redwood-managed clusters
- SREs who own capacity SLOs and alerting

Component architecture (high level):
- Terraform module (this repo): creates spot and on-demand instance pools, ASG/Managed Instance Group configs, instance templates, IAM roles, and controller config stored in k8s ConfigMap/Secret.
- Cluster controller (K8s operator/cron job): watches node pool metrics and PodQueue metrics; makes scaling decisions and manipulates preferred-pool labels / taints to trigger k8s scheduling and node group scale actions via cloud provider APIs.
- CI/CD pipeline: lints + unit tests + infra integration tests + canary rollouts of module outputs and controller image.
- Monitoring & alerting: Prometheus metrics, Cloud provider capacity metrics, incident channels in #infra-oncall.

When to use this module:
- Clusters running cost-sensitive inference workloads that are tolerant to transient preemption with fallback requirements (e.g., online inference with <N sec cold-start tolerance, or batch workloads with SLAs).
- Projects that require a deterministic fallback plan to on-demand capacity when spot is unreliable.

Terraform module interface (summary):

| Variable | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---:|---|
| name_prefix | string | "redwood-gsfa" | Unique prefix for resources |
| region | string | - | Cloud region |
| cluster_name | string | - | Target cluster for node labels/tags |
| spot_instance_types | list(string) | ["a100","a10x"] | Preferred spot GPU families (cloud-specific SKU names) |
| on_demand_instance_types | list(string) | ["a100"] | Fallback instance types |
| max_spot_capacity | number | 100 | Desired maximum spot nodes (count) |
| max_on_demand_capacity | number | 50 | Desired maximum on-demand nodes (count) |
| min_spot_capacity | number | 0 | Minimum spot nodes to keep |
| max_on_demand_fraction | number | 0.3 | Max fraction of traffic to serve on on-demand for cost control |
| interruption_risk_threshold | number | 0.25 | Fractional spot-interruption probability above which to shift workloads |
| scale_cooldown_seconds | number | 90 | Debounce for scale actions

Example Terraform usage snippet:

```
module "gsfa" {
  source = "git::ssh://git@github.com/redwood-infra/terraform-gsfa.git//modules/gsfa?ref=v0.9.2"
  name_prefix = "prod-eu-gsfa"
  region = "eu-west-1"
  cluster_name = "redwood-prod-eu"
  spot_instance_types = ["g5.xlarge", "g5.2xlarge"]
  on_demand_instance_types = ["g5.8xlarge"]
  max_spot_capacity = 200
  max_on_demand_capacity = 80
  max_on_demand_fraction = 0.2
}
```

Controller configuration (ConfigMap example):

```
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: gsfa-config
  namespace: redwood-platform
data:
  policy.yaml: |
    evaluation_interval: 30s
    scale_cooldown: 90s
    interruption_risk_threshold: 0.25
    on_demand_fallback_min: 5
```

CI/CD and testing workflow:
1) terraform fmt + validate + tflint run in pre-commit and CI.
2) unit tests for terraform (terratest) that validate module outputs and lifecycle behaviors.
3) infra-integration job (run in ephemeral project account) that applies module with small sizes and validates resources are created and the controller pod can reconcile.
4) controller image build pipeline: build -> static analysis -> integration tests against a test cluster with a simulated spot-interruption injector.
5) Canary release steps: apply terraform module change in staging cluster, deploy controller image to staging, run synthetic workload (see Testing section). If metrics OK for 24 hours, promote module/tag to prod release.

Operational runbook (oncall procedures):
Priority: maintain ability to serve inference traffic within policy SLOs while minimizing cost.

Primary alerts to own:
- GSFA:PendingPodsHigh (PROM): pending_pod_count > 20 for 5m in production inference queue.
- GSFA:SpotInterruptionRate (PROM): spot_interruption_rate > 0.15 for 10m in a region.
- GSFA:OnDemandThrottle (CLOUD): on_demand_pool_scale_errors > 3 in 15m.
- GSFA:NodeUnschedulable (K8S): unschedulable_nodes > 0 for more than 5m for pools labeled "gsfa-fallback".

Alert thresholds and recommended first actions (table):

| Alert | Threshold | First action | Escalation |
|---|---:|---|---|
| PendingPodsHigh | >20 for 5m | Check pending pods (kubectl get pods -A -o wide), inspect scheduler events; identify if due to insufficient GPU nodes | Page infra oncall if not resolved in 10m |
| SpotInterruptionRate | >15% for 10m | Check cloud spot metrics for region; if sustained, increase interruption_risk_threshold or expand on_demand_fallback | Page capacity-team after 30m |
| OnDemandThrottle | >3 API errors in 15m | Check cloud account quotas and rate limits; verify IAM role used by autoscaler has permissions; open cloud support if quota hit | Pager to cloud-ops |

Runbook: Step-by-step restore flow:
1) Triage: open incident channel #infra-oncall and document region, cluster, alert timestamps.
2) Inspect pending pods: `kubectl get pods -n inference -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,STATUS:.status.phase,NODE:.spec.nodeName --field-selector status.phase=Pending`
3) Inspect node pools: `kubectl get nodes -l redwood.gsa/pool -o wide` and cloud console for ASG/Managed Instance Group desired/available counts.
4) If nodes are not provisioning: check cloud API errors, examine terraform-provisioned ASG health and scaling events. If scale launch failures (insufficient quota, IP limit), follow cloud-specific quota escalation steps (appendix).
5) To temporarily prioritize capacity: manually increase on_demand_capacity via terraform `tf apply -var='max_on_demand_capacity=XXX'` or run the quick-toggle script in `/opt/infra-scripts/gsfa-toggle-on-demand.sh` (requires infra-admin role). Document the change in the incident channel.
6) If spot interruption risk is high and automated fallback not triggering: set `interruption_risk_threshold` in the controller ConfigMap to a lower value (e.g., from 0.25 -> 0.15) and restart controller pod: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/gsfa-controller -n redwood-platform`. Monitor for reconciliation within 2 minutes.
7) When capacity is restored, reverse any manual on-demand increases and revert controller config change; record all actions in incident log and postmortem if incident > 1 hour.

Rollback steps (if a Terraform module change caused the issue):
1) Revert module reference to previous released tag (example: v0.9.1) in infra repo, run `terraform plan` in staging.
2) If verified, apply revert in prod using the standard terraform-production workflow (require two approvers).
3) If revert is not possible because of state drift, follow the manual remediation steps above and open a follow-up engineering ticket for state reconciliation.

Testing checklist (pre-deploy):
- [ ] Unit tests for module outputs (terratest) pass in CI.
- [ ] Integration apply in ephemeral test account completes without errors.
- [ ] Controller image passes integration tests with simulated spot interruptions (we provide an injector job in test-nightly namespace).
- [ ] Synthetic workload: run 1000 inference requests across spot-on-demand ratio and verify 95th pct queue wait < 30s.
- [ ] Cost simulation: run cost estimate job to ensure expected spot savings >= 20% before rollout.

SLOs and KPIs to monitor:
- Capacity SLO: 95th percentile queue wait time for inference <= 30s.
- Availability SLO: < 0.5% of inference requests error with scheduling-related failures due to capacity over a 30d window.
- Cost KPI: realized spot usage fraction >= target (configurable by team) over a billing cycle.

CI/CD knobs and approvals:
- All module changes require two approvers from infra-team and one from platform-sre.
- Breaking changes to the controller's reconciliation model must include a migration plan and compatibility tests.
- Canary window: 24h synthetic traffic + daily health checks for 7 days before full promotion.

Security and IAM notes:
- Terraform module creates a least-privilege role used by the controller. Review IAM changes for `iam:Create*` and `ec2:RunInstances` style permissions during code review.
- Secrets required for cloud API keys must be stored in the Vault path `secret/infra/gsfa/<env>` and referenced only by the controller ServiceAccount with bound K8s Secret.

Appendix A — Common CLI snippets:
- Check pending pods: `kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide --field-selector=status.phase=Pending`
- Describe a problematic pod: `kubectl describe pod <pod-name> -n inference`
- Check gsfa controller logs: `kubectl logs -l app=gsfa-controller -n redwood-platform --since=1h`
- Quick toggle script (infra-admin only): `/opt/infra-scripts/gsfa-toggle-on-demand.sh --increase 20`

Appendix B — Cloud quota and limits quick references:
- EC2 GPU instance quota: check consoles for `Elastic GPU cores` and `On-demand GPU cores`. If quota exhausted, file support ticket with cloud provider and reference internal quota request template `templates/cloud-quota-request.md`.
- Subnet IP exhaustion: ensure node pools use secondary subnets with sufficient /24 blocks; if not, coordinate with networking to allocate new subnets.

Ownership and contacts:
- Module owner: platform-infra (team) — primary: Miguel Ortega (miguel@redwood.ai)
- Controller owner: serving-runtime infra — primary: Priya Nair (priya@redwood.ai)
- Oncall escalation: #infra-oncall slack, pager duty infra-sre

If you are changing terraform inputs that affect production capacity, notify #infra-deployments and obtain signoff from platform-sre before applying in prod.
